document.title: NASA FY 2024 Agency Financial Report
document.license: Work of the U.S. Government (NASA) - public domain in the U.S. (17 U.S.C. 105); NASA media guidelines apply to logos/insignia.
document.page_numbering: All 'page' values are PDF page indices (1-based). Printed page number = PDF page - 1 for pages 2-126.

frozen: 2026-11-14, written before any advanced-pipeline experiment; evidence checked by viewing the rendered original pages
scoring: Answerable: PASS only if answer is correct and complete (values, units, conditions, arithmetic) AND citations point to every required evidence page (multi-hop: all listed pages) AND cited content supports the whole answer. No-evidence: PASS only if the agent abstains or states lack of evidence without unsupported claims. Errors/timeouts = FAIL, kept in the denominator.

questions.question: On NASA's Consolidated Balance Sheet, what was the Fund Balance with Treasury as of September 30, 2024 and as of September 30, 2023?

questions.question: According to the Consolidated Statements of Net Cost, how much earned revenue did Strategic Goal 1 have in FY 2024 and FY 2023?

questions.question: In the Combined Statements of Budgetary Resources, what were NASA's total New Obligations and Upward Adjustments in FY 2024, and how did that compare with FY 2023?
questions.answer: $27,170 million in FY 2024 versus $28,276 million in FY 2023 (a decrease of $1,106 million).

evidence.region: table: Combined Statements of Budgetary Resources, row 'New Obligations and Upward Adjustments (Total)'
evidence.quote: New Obligations and Upward Adjustments (Total) $ 27,170 $ 28,276

questions.question: In the Grants Programs Information table, how many grants/cooperative agreements expired 2-3 years ago still had undisbursed balances, and what was the total undisbursed amount for that age band?

questions.question: Which contract/instrument type accounted for the largest percentage of NASA Office of Procurement obligations in FY 2024, and what was the second largest?
questions.answer: Firm-Fixed-Price at 31%; second was Cost-Plus-Award-Fee at 28%.

evidence.region: table: Instrument Type / Percentage of Total Obligations (Procurement - Oversight)
evidence.quote: Firm-Fixed-Price 31% Cost-Plus-Award-Fee 28% Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee 23%

questions.question: In NASA's organizational chart, which boxes are attached to the Administrator's office with dotted lines, and what do the dotted lines indicate?
questions.answer: Advisory Groups (NAC & ASAP) and the Inspector General; dotted lines indicate independent advisory or oversight organizations.

evidence.region: figure: organizational chart, upper-left boxes + legend
evidence.quote: Dotted lines indicate independent advisory or oversight organizations

questions.question: In Figure 2 (NASA's UNICORN enterprise risk management diagram), which five risk categories are shown in the colored band beneath the councils?
questions.answer: Political and Reputational Risk, Programmatic Risk, Financial Risk, Strategic Risk, and Operational Risk.

evidence.region: figure: Figure 2 NASA's UNICORN, colored band in lower half
evidence.quote: Political and Reputational Risk | Programmatic Risk | Financial Risk | Strategic Risk | Operational Risk

questions.question: According to the 'NASA's Performance Framework Breakdown' graphic, how many Strategic Goals, Strategic Objectives and Performance Goals does the framework contain?
questions.answer: 4 Strategic Goals, 12 Strategic Objectives and 50 Performance Goals.

evidence.region: figure: NASA's Performance Framework Breakdown graphic
evidence.quote: 04 Strategic Goals | 12 Strategic Objectives | 50 Performance Goals

questions.question: In the photo of the Artemis II crew posing with White House staff, who is the Canadian Space Agency astronaut and where is he positioned in the photo?

questions.question: On the 'Testing Capabilities Support Future Mission Success' page, which spacecraft is shown being inspected inside the Payload Hazardous Servicing Facility, and what will it help determine?
questions.answer: Europa Clipper; it will help determine whether conditions below the surface of Jupiter's moon Europa could support life.

evidence.region: photo + caption: Payload Hazardous Servicing Facility at Kennedy Space Center
evidence.quote: inspect the Agency's largest planetary mission spacecraft, Europa Clipper ... will help determine if conditions exist below the surface Jupiter's fourth largest moon, Europa that could support life

questions.question: By how much did Strategic Goal 1's net cost change from FY 2023 to FY 2024, and what single theme word does NASA use for Strategic Goal 1?
questions.answer: It decreased by $224 million (from $8,262 million to $8,038 million); the theme word is DISCOVER.

evidence.region: table: Statement of Net Cost, Strategic Goal 1 'Net Costs' row
evidence.quote: Net Costs 8,038 8,262

evidence.region: text: four major themes

questions.question: Which independent public accounting firm audited NASA's FY 2024 financial statements, and what material weakness did the audit summary report?
questions.answer: Ernst & Young LLP (EY), under contract with the NASA OIG; one material weakness: Deficiencies in Financial Reporting Oversight Controls.

evidence.region: text: Letter from the Inspector General on Audit
evidence.quote: contracted with the independent public accounting firm Ernst & Young LLP (EY) to audit NASA's fiscal year (FY) 2024 financial statements

evidence.region: table: Summary of Financial Statement Audit
evidence.quote: Deficiencies in Financial Reporting Oversight Controls

questions.question: Why did the 'Other' category of NASA's assets increase by $881 million in FY 2024?
questions.answer: Because of a new Agency business process for lease accounting mandated by SFFAS 54, Leases, which requires additional financial reporting for leases.

evidence.region: text: paragraph below the asset charts
evidence.quote: This category increased by $881 million. This increase is due to the implementation of a new Agency business process for lease accounting mandated by the Statement of Federal Financial Accounting Standards (SFFAS) 54, Leases

questions.question: Following the findings of the internal Agency Risk Management Tiger Team, what position did NASA establish and within which office?
questions.answer: An Agency Risk Management Officer (ARMO), within the Headquarters Office of Safety and Mission Assurance.

evidence.region: text: Enterprise Risk Management, second paragraph
evidence.quote: establishment of an Agency Risk Management Officer (ARMO) within the Headquarters Office of Safety and Mission Assurance

questions.question: When and by which law was NASA established, and what was its predecessor agency?
questions.answer: Established by Congress on October 1, 1958 by the National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958; predecessor: the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics (NACA).

evidence.region: text: Reporting Entity
evidence.quote: established by Congress on October 1, 1958 by the National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958. NASA was incorporated from its predecessor agency, the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics

questions.question: Of the funds available to NASA in FY 2024, how much did NASA obligate, and what happens to the remaining amount?
questions.answer: NASA obligated $27 billion of the $30 billion available; the remaining $3 billion may be obligated until the funds' periods of availability expire.

evidence.region: text: Sources of Funding, paragraph above the charts
evidence.quote: NASA obligated $27 billion of the $30 billion available ... The remaining $3 billion may be obligated until the funds' periods of availability expire.

questions.question: In the photo on the Mission Performance page, what is astronaut Kate Rubins doing and why is that tool important?
questions.answer: Using a hammer to get a drive tube into the ground to collect a pristine soil sample during a nighttime simulated moonwalk; the drive tube preserves the integrity of lunar samples.

evidence.region: photo + caption
evidence.quote: uses a hammer to get a drive tube into the ground to collect a pristine soil sample ... The drive tube is the key piece of hardware for preserving the integrity of samples from the Moon.

questions.question: According to the Net Cost of Operations discussion, how much earned revenue did NASA have in FY 2024 and how did its net cost change from FY 2023?
questions.answer: Earned revenue was $1.8 billion (up $200 million); net cost was $24.7 billion, an increase of $118 million.

evidence.region: text: Net Cost of Operations paragraph
evidence.quote: Earned Revenue ... was $1.8 billion, a $200 million increase from FY 2023. This leaves NASA with a FY 2024 net cost of $24.7 billion, an increase of $118 million

questions.question: What do NASA's Environmental and Disposal Liabilities represent, and how much did they change in FY 2024?
questions.answer: They are the estimated cost to clean up known and projected environmental hazards; $2.4 billion, an increase of $48 million (2%).

evidence.region: text: Total Liabilities paragraph
evidence.quote: Environmental and Disposal Liabilities of $2.4 billion represent the estimated cost to clean up both known and projected environmental hazards. This category had an increase of $48 million or two percent.

questions.question: Through compliance with which two laws does NASA demonstrate stewardship of its resources and accountability for results?
questions.answer: The Chief Financial Officers Act of 1990 (CFO Act) and the GPRA Modernization Act of 2010 (GPRAMA).

evidence.region: text: Welcome to NASA
evidence.quote: compliance with the Chief Financial Officers Act of 1990 (CFO Act) and the Government Performance and Results Act Modernization Act of 2010 (GPRAMA)
